name: addpipe16_flat_cla_sop
rationale: All prior hand-built hierarchical adders (bit-level Kogge-Stone, mux-based conditional-sum, block CLA4, carry-select variants) imposed artificial RTL-level structural boundaries (block G/P merges, mux trees, generate hierarchies) and every one of them underperformed the plain native '+' baseline, even though they are logically equivalent. This suggests that imposed hierarchy/boundaries in the RTL are preventing ABC's resynthesis (balance/resub/rewrite) from reaching the same optimum that native $add mapping reaches. This candidate instead expresses the entire 16-bit carry-lookahead as a single flat, fully-expanded sum-of-products for every carry bit (c[i] = OR_j (g[j] & AND_{k=j+1..i} p[k])), with no intermediate named hierarchical block-carry signals and no iterative doubling structure imposed. This gives Yosys/ABC maximum freedom to structurally hash, share, and re-balance the whole carry network from scratch, which for a circuit this small (16-bit adder) is well within ABC's resynthesis capability, and may let it discover a mapping as good as (or closer to) the native-inferred one rather than being locked into a suboptimal user-imposed topology, unlike all previous attempts.
